name: Eyjafjallajökull
description: In 2010 this glacier-capped volcano grounded roughly 100,000 flights and stranded millions of travellers. Meltwater flooding the vent shattered the magma into unusually fine, abrasive ash that drifted across European airspace for days.
geology: Located along Iceland's volcanic rift zone, Eyjafjallajökull is shaped by the interaction between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates.

name: Mount Fuji
description: Japan's sacred icon last erupted in 1707, dusting Edo (modern Tokyo) with ash 100 km away. Its near-perfect cone has been a pilgrimage site for centuries and the muse behind Hokusai's famous woodblock prints.
geology: The stratovolcano is located on the Pacific ring of fire, at a triple junction between the Pacific, Phillipine and Eurasian plate.

name: Kilauea
description: Home of the fire goddess Pele, Kilauea's Halemaʻumaʻu crater has held lava lakes on and off for centuries. Its 2018 eruption drained the summit and sent lava through Leilani Estates, destroying over 700 homes.
geology: The shield volcano is fed by the Hawaiian hotspot - a lone mantle plume in the centre of the pacific plate.

name: Mount St. Helens
description: On 18 May 1980 the mountain's north face collapsed in the largest landslide in recorded history, unleashing a sideways blast that flattened forest across roughly 600 square km and killed 57 people. The summit dropped by about 400 m.
geology: The Volcano sits above the Cascadia Subduction Zone, where the partial melting of the Juan de Fuca plate results in magma-fuelled eruptions.

name: Etna
description: Europe's tallest active volcano has been erupting for around half a million years, regularly staging lava fountains over Sicily and coating Catania in ash. Its summit craters reshape themselves with almost every major eruption.
geology: Etna is a complex stratovolcano formed by the collision of the African and Eurasian plates, fueling its highly active and fluid magma system.

name: Krakatoa
description: The 1883 eruption was heard roughly 4,800 km away and its tsunamis killed over 36,000 people. Today the young island of Anak Krakatau ('Child of Krakatoa') grows from the drowned caldera, and its 2018 flank collapse triggered another deadly wave.
geology: Krakatoa lives on through Anak Krakatau ('Child of Krakatoa'), which demonstrates frequent, small eruptions.

name: Ojos del Salado
description: At 6,893 m this is the highest active volcano on Earth, straddling the Chile-Argentina border in the bone-dry Atacama. Its summit crater holds what is considered the highest lake in the world, at about 6,390 m.
geology: Ojos del Salado is a complex stratovolcano formed by the subduction of the Nazca plate beneath the South American plate.

name: Mount Kilimanjaro
description: Africa's highest mountain is a free-standing giant built from three volcanoes: Kibo, Mawenzi and Shira. Kibo is dormant rather than extinct and still vents gas, while the famous summit glaciers are rapidly shrinking.
geology: Mount Kilimanjaro is a complex stratovolcano formed by the East African Rift system, the same system responsible for most african volcanism today..

name: Mount Vesuvius
description: The volcano that buried Pompeii and Herculaneum in AD 79 still looms over the Bay of Naples. It last erupted in 1944, and roughly 600,000 people now live in its red zone, making it one of the most closely watched volcanoes on Earth.
geology: Vesuvius is a complex stratovolcano formed by the subduction of the African plate beneath the Eurasian plate in the Mediterranean region.

name: Mount Elbrus
description: The twin-peaked giant of the Caucasus is the highest mountain in Europe by the usual boundary. Its summits are covered in glaciers that feed several major rivers, though the volcano itself has been quiet for around 2,000 years.
geology: Elbrus is a complex stratovolcano formed by the subduction of the Arabian plate beneath the Eurasian plate.

name: Mount Pelee
description: In May 1902 a glowing pyroclastic flow swept down and destroyed the port of Saint-Pierre in minutes, killing roughly 28,000 people. The disaster defined 'Peléan' eruptions and is one of the deadliest volcanic events of the 20th century.
geology: Pelee is a complex stratovolcano formed by the subduction of the North American plate beneath the Caribbean plate.

name: Mount Merapi
description: Indonesia's 'Mountain of Fire' sits just north of Yogyakarta, and its steep lava dome regularly collapses into fast-moving pyroclastic flows. The 2010 eruption killed more than 350 people and displaced around 350,000.
geology: Merapi is a complex stratovolcano formed by the subduction of the Indo-Australian plate beneath the Eurasian plate.

name: Mount Warning
description: The worn-down plug of a vast shield volcano that erupted about 23 million years ago. A ring of mountains around it marks the eroded caldera, and this hard-rock core is all that remains of the central vent.
geology: Mount Warning is a shield volcano formed by the eruption of basaltic lava flows during the Miocene epoch.

name: Mount Erebus
description: The world's southernmost active volcano rises from Antarctica's Ross Island and has held a lava lake of molten phonolite for decades. Its summit is studded with ice towers built by freezing volcanic steam.
geology: Erebus is a complex stratovolcano formed by the subduction of the Pacific plate beneath the Antarctic plate.

name: Mount Rainier
description: Draped in around 25 glaciers, Rainier looms over Seattle and Tacoma. Its real threat is lahars: volcanic mudflows from melting ice that could race down valleys into populated areas, which is why it is rated among the most dangerous volcanoes in the US.
geology: Rainier is a complex stratovolcano formed by the subduction of the Juan de Fuca plate beneath the North American plate.

name: Mount Shasta
description: One of the largest stratovolcanoes in the Cascades, Shasta towers over northern California. Its Shastina cone is a volcano in its own right, and the mountain has long been sacred to the region's Native peoples.
geology: Shasta is a complex stratovolcano formed by the subduction of the Juan de Fuca plate beneath the North American plate.

name: Mount Teide
description: Spain's highest peak rises over 7,000 m from the Atlantic seabed, making it one of the tallest volcanic structures on Earth. The Guanche people of Tenerife believed the demon Guayota lived inside it.
geology: Teide is a complex stratovolcano formed by the interaction of the African and Eurasian tectonic plates.

name: Mount Ruapehu
description: The North Island's highest peak holds a steaming, acidic crater lake. In 1953 that lake burst through its rim, and the resulting lahar swept away a rail bridge at Tangiwai, killing 151 people on a passing train.
geology: Ruapehu is a complex stratovolcano formed by the subduction of the Pacific plate beneath the Australian plate.

name: Arenal
description: Costa Rica's textbook cone erupted violently in 1968, destroying villages, then ran in near-continuous activity for 42 years, glowing red at night. It fell quiet in 2010 and is now wrapped in rainforest and hot springs.
geology: Arenal is part of the volcanic system of Alajuela. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Poás
description: Among the largest active craters in the world, Poás holds a steaming turquoise acid lake over a hot, gassy vent. Acid rain from the plume scorches surrounding vegetation, and sudden steam-driven blasts can occur.
geology: Poás is part of the volcanic system of Alajuela. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Irazú
description: Costa Rica's highest volcano has a green crater lake and, on clear days, views of both the Pacific and Caribbean. Its 1963 eruption began the day US President Kennedy visited, and ash fell on San José for two years.
geology: Irazú is part of the volcanic system of Cartago. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Turrialba
description: Quiet for roughly 150 years, Turrialba woke up from 2010 and began belching ash that repeatedly shut San José's international airport. Its summit craters are still steaming and unstable.
geology: Turrialba is part of the volcanic system of Cartago. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Rincón de la Vieja
description: A steaming mountain of mud pots, fumaroles and hot springs, topped by a hot acidic crater lake. Rincón de la Vieja is best known for small steam-driven explosions that can come with little warning.
geology: Rincón de la Vieja is part of the volcanic system of Guanacaste. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Fuego
description: Guatemala's 'Volcano of Fire' erupts almost continuously, with explosions every hour or so visible from the colonial city of Antigua. On 3 June 2018 pyroclastic flows swept through villages on its flanks, killing hundreds.
geology: Fuego is part of the volcanic system of Chimaltenango / Escuintla. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Pacaya
description: A popular volcano for hikers, who can roast marshmallows on warm lava rocks near the summit. Pacaya has been erupting more or less continuously since 1961, and an eruption in 2010 closed the capital's airport.
geology: Pacaya is part of the volcanic system of Escuintla. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Santiaguito
description: A volcano growing inside another's crater: Santiaguito began as a lava dome in the hole blasted from Santa María in 1902. It has been extruding lava and exploding almost daily since 1922.
geology: Santiaguito is part of the volcanic system of Quetzaltenango. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Santa María
description: After centuries of silence its 1902 eruption was one of the largest of the 20th century, sending ash across Central America and killing thousands. The blast scooped out a huge crater on the south flank, where Santiaguito now grows.
geology: Santa María is part of the volcanic system of Quetzaltenango. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Izalco
description: Born from a vent in 1770, Izalco erupted so regularly that sailors called it the 'Lighthouse of the Pacific'. It fell silent in 1966, leaving a perfect, steep-sided cone.
geology: Izalco is part of the volcanic system of Sonsonate. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Santa Ana (Ilamatepec)
description: El Salvador's highest volcano cradles a crater lake of hot, acidic, jade-green water. A sudden explosion in 2005 hurled ash and boulders, killing two people and forcing thousands to evacuate.
geology: Santa Ana (Ilamatepec) is part of the volcanic system of Santa Ana. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: San Miguel (Chaparrastique)
description: Known locally as Chaparrastique, this near-perfect cone overlooks the city of San Miguel. It regularly releases gas and small ash explosions, and has produced lava flows within recorded history.
geology: San Miguel (Chaparrastique) is part of the volcanic system of San Miguel. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Masaya
description: Spanish conquistadors called Masaya's glowing crater the 'Mouth of Hell' and a friar erected a cross there in the 16th century to ward off the devil. A lava lake in Santiago crater has come and gone in recent years.
geology: Masaya is part of the volcanic system of Masaya. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Momotombo
description: A steep cone rising from the shore of Lake Managua. Its 1610 eruption helped doom the Spanish colonial city of León Viejo, and its steam now drives a geothermal power station.
geology: Momotombo is part of the volcanic system of León. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Concepción
description: Ometepe Island, in Lake Nicaragua, is made from two volcanoes: the near-perfect active cone of Concepción and the quieter Maderas. Concepción's frequent ash explosions rain down on villages and coffee farms.
geology: Concepción is part of the volcanic system of Ometepe Island. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: San Cristóbal
description: Nicaragua's tallest volcano is the highest point of the Marrabios range, a chain of cones along the Pacific side of the country. It erupts intermittently with ash plumes and explosions that threaten nearby communities.
geology: San Cristóbal is part of the volcanic system of Chinandega. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Taal
description: A volcanic island in a lake inside a giant caldera, on an island: Taal is small but deadly. Its 1911 eruption killed over 1,300 people, and its January 2020 eruption blanketed Manila in ash.
geology: Taal is part of the volcanic system of Batangas. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Mayon
description: Mayon's smooth, almost perfect cone is the Philippines' most iconic volcano. Its 1814 eruption buried the town of Cagsawa and killed over 1,000 people, leaving only the church bell tower standing.
geology: Mayon is part of the volcanic system of Albay. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Pinatubo
description: After 500 years of dormancy, Pinatubo erupted in 1991 in the second-largest eruption of the 20th century. The ash cloud rose around 35 km and cooled global temperatures by about half a degree, while timely evacuations saved thousands of lives.
geology: Pinatubo is part of the volcanic system of Luzon. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Kanlaon
description: The highest peak on Negros Island is one of the Philippines' most active volcanoes. Explosive eruptions have repeatedly forced thousands from their homes and showered nearby farms with ash.
geology: Kanlaon is part of the volcanic system of Negros Island. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Bulusan
description: Located on the southern tip of Luzon, Bulusan is known for frequent small steam-driven explosions that spit ash over villages. It sits inside a natural park along with a serene crater lake.
geology: Bulusan is part of the volcanic system of Sorsogon. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Ruang
description: A small island volcano in the Sangihe chain. Its violent April 2024 eruptions forced thousands to evacuate and raised fears of a tsunami, a real risk after its 1871 eruption caused a collapse-driven wave.
geology: Ruang is part of the volcanic system of Sangihe Islands. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Semeru
description: 'Mahameru', the Great Mountain, is Java's highest peak and erupts almost constantly with ash puffs and pyroclastic flows. In December 2021 a flow buried villages in Lumajang and killed dozens.
geology: Semeru is part of the volcanic system of East Java. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Bromo
description: A smoking cone rising from a vast sea of volcanic sand inside the Tengger caldera. Visitors ride up for the sunrise, and each year Hindu Tenggerese throw offerings into the crater during the Yadnya Kasada festival.
geology: Bromo is part of the volcanic system of East Java. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Ijen
description: At night this crater glows with electric-blue flames from burning sulphuric gas, while miners haul out loads of yellow sulphur. Below sits the largest highly acidic lake in the world, a striking turquoise.
geology: Ijen is part of the volcanic system of East Java. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Agung
description: Bali's highest and holiest mountain, with the island's 'mother temple' Besakih on its slopes. Its 1963 eruption killed about 1,100 people during a major religious ceremony, and ash from 2017-19 closed Bali's airport.
geology: Agung is part of the volcanic system of Bali. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Rinjani
description: Lombok's crater lake, Segara Anak, sits within a giant caldera and a newer cone, Barujari, still grows inside it. The caldera came from the colossal 1257 Samalas eruption, which cooled global climate.
geology: Rinjani is part of the volcanic system of Lombok. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Tambora
description: The 1815 eruption was the largest in recorded history, killing tens of thousands and shrinking the mountain by over 1,000 m. Its ash and sulphur cooled the planet and triggered 1816's 'Year Without a Summer'.
geology: Tambora is part of the volcanic system of Sumbawa. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Soputan
description: One of the most active volcanoes in Sulawesi, Soputan erupts suddenly and explosively, sending ash plumes several kilometres up and lava flows down its sides with little warning.
geology: Soputan is part of the volcanic system of North Sulawesi. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Lokon-Empung
description: Lokon and Empung are side-by-side twin peaks overlooking the city of Tomohon. Frequent small eruptions mean the pair are monitored closely, and the city's residents live daily with ash and tremors.
geology: Lokon-Empung is part of the volcanic system of North Sulawesi. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Kerinci
description: The highest volcano in Indonesia towers over Sumatra's Kerinci Seblat National Park, a rainforest home to Sumatran tigers. It steams and sputters regularly, with small ash eruptions from its crater.
geology: Kerinci is part of the volcanic system of Sumatra. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Sinabung
description: After about 400 years of silence, Sinabung roared back in 2010 and has erupted on and off since. Dome collapses sent pyroclastic flows that killed 16 people in 2014 and seven in 2016, displacing thousands.
geology: Sinabung is part of the volcanic system of North Sumatra. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Marapi
description: A popular climbing mountain in West Sumatra that erupted without warning in December 2023, killing 24 hikers on its slopes. Its steaming summit crater is constantly monitored.
geology: Marapi is part of the volcanic system of West Sumatra. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Dukono
description: Dukono has been erupting almost continuously since 1933, making it one of the longest-running eruptions on Earth. Its ash plume is regularly visible from space above remote Halmahera.
geology: Dukono is part of the volcanic system of Halmahera. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Ibu
description: Ibu has been erupting repeatedly since 2008, sending up ash plumes day after day and growing a lava dome. Authorities keep an exclusion zone around its crater and ash regularly dusts villages.
geology: Ibu is part of the volcanic system of Halmahera. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Lewotobi
description: Lewotobi is a pair of volcanoes: Laki-laki ('husband') and Perempuan ('wife'), less than 2 km apart. A violent eruption of Laki-laki in November 2024 killed around ten people and sent thousands fleeing.
geology: Lewotobi is part of the volcanic system of Flores. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Klyuchevskoy
description: Eurasia's highest active volcano is a near-perfect cone about 6,000 years old. It frequently fires off lava fountains and ash clouds, and sits among a cluster of peaks in Kamchatka's Klyuchevskaya group.
geology: Klyuchevskoy is part of the volcanic system of Kamchatka. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Shiveluch
description: One of Kamchatka's most active volcanoes, Shiveluch repeatedly grows a huge lava dome that collapses in explosions. These blasts send ash plumes high into the North Pacific air routes.
geology: Shiveluch is part of the volcanic system of Kamchatka. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Bezymianny
description: Its name means 'Nameless', because it was thought extinct until it erupted in 1955-56 with a massive sideways blast, a close preview of what Mount St. Helens did 24 years later.
geology: Bezymianny is part of the volcanic system of Kamchatka. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Karymsky
description: Kamchatka's most consistently active cone, erupting small explosions every few minutes. In 1996 an underwater explosion in a nearby caldera lake coincided with a Karymsky eruption, startling volcanologists.
geology: Karymsky is part of the volcanic system of Kamchatka. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Avachinsky
description: Looming over the regional capital Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky, Avachinsky is ranked among the world's 'Decade Volcanoes' because an eruption could be dangerous for such a populated area.
geology: Avachinsky is part of the volcanic system of Kamchatka. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Kronotsky
description: One of Kamchatka's most symmetrical cones, set in a remote wilderness reserve beside Lake Kronotskoye. Its last known eruption was in 1923, and few visitors ever see its snowy summit.
geology: Kronotsky is part of the volcanic system of Kamchatka. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Alaid
description: Alaid is the highest volcano in the Kuril Islands and makes up the whole of Atlasov Island. Its symmetrical cone rises directly from the stormy Sea of Okhotsk.
geology: Alaid is part of the volcanic system of Kuril Islands. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Sarychev Peak
description: This Kuril volcano is famous for a 2009 eruption photographed from the International Space Station. Astronauts captured a pyroclastic flow and ash plume punching through a hole in the cloud layer.
geology: Sarychev Peak is part of the volcanic system of Kuril Islands. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Sakurajima
description: Sakurajima erupts almost daily, dusting the nearby city of Kagoshima with ash so regularly that residents carry umbrellas and keep ash-collection bags. Lava flows in 1914 joined it to the mainland, turning an island into a peninsula.
geology: Sakurajima is part of the volcanic system of Kagoshima Bay. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Aso
description: One of the world's largest calderas, around 25 km across, with towns, farms and railways inside it. Four colossal eruptions between 270,000 and 90,000 years ago formed it, and the central cone of Nakadake still erupts.
geology: Aso is part of the volcanic system of Kyushu. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Unzen
description: In 1991 a lava dome collapse sent a pyroclastic flow down the mountain, killing 43 people including volcanologists Katia and Maurice Krafft. In 1792 a collapse here triggered a tsunami that killed around 15,000 people.
geology: Unzen is part of the volcanic system of Kyushu. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Asama
description: Overlooking the resort town of Karuizawa, Asama is one of Japan's most active volcanoes. Its 1783 Tenmei eruption killed around 1,500 people and contributed to a widespread famine.
geology: Asama is part of the volcanic system of Honshu. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Ontake
description: A sacred pilgrimage mountain, Ontake erupted suddenly at lunchtime on 27 September 2014 with no warning, killing 63 hikers. It remains Japan's deadliest volcanic disaster since the Second World War.
geology: Ontake is part of the volcanic system of Honshu. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Suwanosejima
description: A small remote island whose summit crater has been almost continuously active for decades. Explosions regularly send ash and glowing rocks skyward, while a small community lives on the island.
geology: Suwanosejima is part of the volcanic system of Ryukyu Islands. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Kusatsu-Shirane
description: Famous for the hot-spring town of Kusatsu at its foot, with a strikingly acidic emerald crater lake called Yugama. A sudden 2018 eruption sent rocks onto a ski slope, killing one person.
geology: Kusatsu-Shirane is part of the volcanic system of Honshu. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Changbaishan (Paektu)
description: Straddling the China-North Korea border, this volcano holds Heaven Lake in its summit caldera. Its 'Millennium Eruption' around 946 CE was one of the largest of the last 2,000 years, and the mountain is sacred in Korean and Manchu tradition.
geology: Changbaishan (Paektu) is part of the volcanic system of Changbai Mountains. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Barren Island
description: The only confirmed active volcano in South Asia, a lone island in the Andaman Sea with a flooded caldera opening to the sea. Erupting every few years, it is uninhabited apart from goats and fruit bats.
geology: Barren Island is part of the volcanic system of Andaman Sea. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Bagana
description: Bagana is a remote steep-sided lava cone on Bougainville that has been oozing lava almost continuously for years. It is one of Papua New Guinea's most active volcanoes yet one of its least studied.
geology: Bagana is part of the volcanic system of Bougainville. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Ulawun
description: Papua New Guinea's 'Father' volcano is one of the country's most active and is a Decade Volcano. Its 2019 eruption sent ash 19 km into the sky and forced thousands to evacuate.
geology: Ulawun is part of the volcanic system of New Britain. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Manam
description: An entire island that is a volcano, around 10 km wide with thousands of people living on its flanks. Radial valleys channel pyroclastic flows and lava toward the sea, forcing repeated evacuations.
geology: Manam is part of the volcanic system of Manam Island. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Rabaul
description: A flooded caldera that forms a natural harbour. In 1994 twin eruptions from Tavurvur and Vulcan buried the town of Rabaul in ash, though early evacuation kept the death toll remarkably low.
geology: Rabaul is part of the volcanic system of New Britain. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Yasur
description: Yasur has been erupting almost non-stop for at least 800 years, and Captain Cook saw its glow in 1774. Visitors can walk to its rim at night and watch lava bombs burst above them.
geology: Yasur is part of the volcanic system of Tanna Island. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Ambrym
description: Ambrym is a huge caldera with twin lava lakes in Marum and Benbow craters. A 2018 rift eruption drained the lakes and forced people from their villages, and the island is known for its carved ritual figures.
geology: Ambrym is part of the volcanic system of Ambrym Island. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Lopevi
description: A near-perfect cone that makes up a whole island in Vanuatu. Lopevi erupts frequently, sending ash plumes and lava toward the sea, and nobody lives on it permanently.
geology: Lopevi is part of the volcanic system of Lopevi Island. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Whakaari / White Island
description: New Zealand's most active volcano is a mostly submerged cone 48 km offshore, once mined for sulphur. In December 2019 a sudden eruption killed 22 people who were visiting the island.
geology: Whakaari / White Island is part of the volcanic system of Bay of Plenty. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Taranaki / Egmont
description: Taranaki is a snow-capped, near-symmetrical cone. Māori legend tells that it lost a fight with Tongariro over the mountain Pihanga and fled west to the coast. Its last known eruption was in 1854.
geology: Taranaki / Egmont is part of the volcanic system of North Island. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Tongariro
description: A World Heritage volcanic massif and the setting for the famous Tongariro Alpine Crossing. It includes Ngauruhoe, which played Mount Doom in the Lord of the Rings films, and a 2012 eruption hurled boulders onto the hiking trail.
geology: Tongariro is part of the volcanic system of North Island. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Hekla
description: Medieval Europeans called Hekla the 'Gateway to Hell'. Since 1970 it has erupted roughly every ten years, often with only minutes of warning, and its long ridge looks like an upturned boat.
geology: Hekla is part of the volcanic system of Southern Iceland. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Katla
description: Katla hides beneath the Mýrdalsjökull ice cap, and its eruptions melt ice into enormous meltwater floods. Its last major eruption was in 1918, so it is considered overdue and is closely monitored.
geology: Katla is part of the volcanic system of Southern Iceland. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Grímsvötn
description: Iceland's most frequently erupting volcano lies beneath the Vatnajökull ice cap. Its subglacial lake periodically bursts out as huge floods, and its 2011 eruption sent an ash plume that shut down Icelandic airspace.
geology: Grímsvötn is part of the volcanic system of Vatnajökull. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Bárðarbunga
description: A vast ice-buried volcano whose 2014-15 Holuhraun eruption lasted six months, the largest in Iceland since 1783. As the magma drained away, the caldera floor sank around 65 m.
geology: Bárðarbunga is part of the volcanic system of Vatnajökull. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Askja
description: A remote highland caldera holding the deep, cold lake Öskjuvatn. Its 1875 eruption dusted Scandinavia with ash, and Apollo astronauts trained here in the 1960s for the Moon landings.
geology: Askja is part of the volcanic system of Central Highlands. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Krafla
description: Krafla's 'Fires' of 1975-84 split the ground with nine eruptions and rifting. Today a geothermal power station harnesses its heat, and in 2009 a drill hole accidentally struck liquid magma.
geology: Krafla is part of the volcanic system of Northern Iceland. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Fagradalsfjall
description: After around 800 years of silence the Reykjanes Peninsula woke up in March 2021, with lava from Fagradalsfjall flowing in a valley within hiking distance of Reykjavik. Thousands of visitors came to watch.
geology: Fagradalsfjall is part of the volcanic system of Reykjanes Peninsula. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Beerenberg
description: The northernmost active volcano above sea level on Earth, standing on remote Jan Mayen in the Arctic Ocean. Glaciers pour down its flanks right into the sea.
geology: Beerenberg is part of the volcanic system of Jan Mayen. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Stromboli
description: Known as the 'Lighthouse of the Mediterranean', Stromboli has erupted almost continuously for at least 2,000 years, with small explosions every few minutes. It gave its name to 'Strombolian' eruptions worldwide.
geology: Stromboli is part of the volcanic system of Aeolian Islands. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Vulcano
description: The Romans believed this island was the chimney of the forge of Vulcan, god of fire, giving the world the word 'volcano'. Today it steams with sulphur vents and mud baths, and last erupted from 1888 to 1890.
geology: Vulcano is part of the volcanic system of Aeolian Islands. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Campi Flegrei
description: A supervolcano beside Naples: a caldera about 12 km wide, formed by giant eruptions around 39,000 and 15,000 years ago. The ground has risen by metres in recent decades, and about 500,000 people live inside it.
geology: Campi Flegrei is part of the volcanic system of Campania. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Ischia
description: A volcanic island in the Bay of Naples, famed for its thermal spas. Its last eruption was in 1302, but the 1883 earthquake at Casamicciola, caused by the same geology, killed around 2,300 people.
geology: Ischia is part of the volcanic system of Tyrrhenian Sea. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Santorini
description: The Minoan eruption around 1600 BCE was one of the largest in human history. It left a flooded caldera ringed by cliffs and white-washed towns, and may have inspired the legend of Atlantis.
geology: Santorini is part of the volcanic system of Cyclades. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Nisyros
description: A small round island in Greece with a hot caldera and a crater, Stefanos, where steam explosions have happened. Myth says Poseidon created Nisyros by throwing a chunk of Kos at the giant Polybotes.
geology: Nisyros is part of the volcanic system of Dodecanese. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Ararat
description: Turkey's highest peak is an ice-capped giant long said to be the resting place of Noah's Ark. In 1840 an eruption and earthquake triggered landslides that buried a village on its slope.
geology: Ararat is part of the volcanic system of Eastern Anatolia. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Nemrut
description: A large caldera with crater lakes and hot springs overlooking Lake Van. Not to be confused with Nemrut Dağ and its statues, this volcano last erupted in 1692 and still steams.
geology: Nemrut is part of the volcanic system of Eastern Anatolia. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Damavand
description: The highest volcano in Asia at 5,610 m, topped by sulphurous fumaroles. In Persian legend the tyrant Zahhak is chained inside it by the hero Fereydun.
geology: Damavand is part of the volcanic system of Alborz Mountains. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Nyiragongo
description: Nyiragongo's lava lake is one of the world's most spectacular, and its lava is so runny that it can flow at highway speeds. Lava reached the city of Goma in 2002, and its 2021 eruption forced hundreds of thousands to flee.
geology: Nyiragongo is part of the volcanic system of Virunga Mountains. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Nyamuragira
description: Africa's most active volcano, erupting every few years and flooding huge lava fields across Virunga National Park. Its wide shield sits close to Nyiragongo and mountain gorilla habitat.
geology: Nyamuragira is part of the volcanic system of Virunga Mountains. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Ol Doinyo Lengai
description: The Maasai call it the 'Mountain of God'. It is the only volcano in the world that erupts natrocarbonatite lava, a cool, black, runny liquid that turns white after rain.
geology: Ol Doinyo Lengai is part of the volcanic system of East African Rift. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Mount Cameroon
description: West Africa's highest peak, locally known as 'Mongo ma Ndemi' (Mountain of Greatness). It erupts every decade or two, and is the site of the annual 'Race of Hope' running event.
geology: Mount Cameroon is part of the volcanic system of Southwest Region. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Pico do Fogo
description: A 2,829 m cone rising from within a vast caldera on Fogo island. A 2014-15 eruption destroyed the villages of Portela and Bangaeira, though everyone escaped, and farmers there grow wine inside the crater.
geology: Pico do Fogo is part of the volcanic system of Fogo Island. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Piton de la Fournaise
description: One of the most active volcanoes on Earth, erupting every year or two, often with lava flows spilling toward the ocean. In 2007 the summit crater Dolomieu collapsed about 300 m.
geology: Piton de la Fournaise is part of the volcanic system of Réunion. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Erta Ale
description: The 'Smoking Mountain' in the Afar language, set in the scorching Danakil Depression. It's one of the few volcanoes with a long-lived lava lake, and has been glowing for more than a century.
geology: Erta Ale is part of the volcanic system of Afar Region. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Cotopaxi
description: A glacier-capped, near-perfect cone more than 5,800 m high and one of the world's highest active volcanoes. Eruptions melt its ice into lahars that could reach Latacunga, and in 1877 mudflows travelled around 100 km towards the coast.
geology: Cotopaxi is part of the volcanic system of Andes. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Chimborazo
description: Chimborazo's summit is the farthest point on Earth's surface from the planet's centre, thanks to the equatorial bulge, beating Everest by around two kilometres. Humboldt tried to climb it in 1802.
geology: Chimborazo is part of the volcanic system of Andes. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Tungurahua
description: Its name means 'Throat of Fire' in Quechua. After waking in 1999 it forced evacuations from nearby Baños, and it was almost constantly erupting until 2016.
geology: Tungurahua is part of the volcanic system of Andes. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Sangay
description: One of the most continuously active volcanoes on Earth, erupting almost non-stop since 1934. It sits in a remote UNESCO national park, with terrain ranging from jungle to snow.
geology: Sangay is part of the volcanic system of Andes. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Reventador
description: Reventador, 'The Exploder', has been erupting since 2002, sending incandescent rocks and lava down its flank. Lahars and ash have damaged nearby roads and oil pipelines.
geology: Reventador is part of the volcanic system of Andes. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Pichincha
description: Quito, Ecuador's capital, nestles on the eastern slope of this volcano. Guagua Pichincha dusted the city with ash in 1999-2002, and in 1822 the Battle of Pichincha, fought on its slopes, sealed Ecuador's independence.
geology: Pichincha is part of the volcanic system of Andes. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Nevado del Ruiz
description: In 1985 a small eruption melted the glacier cap and sent lahars that buried the town of Armero, killing more than 23,000 people. Warnings went unheeded, and the tragedy changed volcano hazard monitoring worldwide.
geology: Nevado del Ruiz is part of the volcanic system of Andes. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Galeras
description: Colombia's volcano near Pasto, a Decade Volcano. In 1993 it exploded while scientists were inside the crater during a conference, killing six scientists and three tourists.
geology: Galeras is part of the volcanic system of Nariño. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Nevado del Huila
description: Colombia's highest volcano at 5,364 m, mantled in glaciers. Eruptions in 2007-08 generated lahars that tore through the Páez River valley, destroying bridges and homes.
geology: Nevado del Huila is part of the volcanic system of Andes. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Villarrica
description: One of the few volcanoes with a persistent lava lake, glowing above the resort town of Pucón. Its Mapuche name, Rukapillán, means 'House of the Spirit', and its snowy cone attracts skiers and climbers.
geology: Villarrica is part of the volcanic system of Araucanía. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Llaima
description: One of Chile's biggest and most active volcanoes, above Conguillío National Park with its ancient araucaria forests. A 2008-09 eruption sent lava flows down its flank and spread ash over nearby towns.
geology: Llaima is part of the volcanic system of Araucanía. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Calbuco
description: After 43 years of silence, Calbuco erupted without warning in April 2015, sending an ash column about 15 km high. Thousands were evacuated and ash fell across Patagonia into Argentina.
geology: Calbuco is part of the volcanic system of Los Lagos. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Osorno
description: A symmetrical, snow-capped cone that rises above Lake Llanquihue and is often compared to Mount Fuji. Its last known eruption was in 1869, and today skiers and hikers flock to it.
geology: Osorno is part of the volcanic system of Los Lagos. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Lascar
description: The most active volcano in northern Chile. A huge 1993 eruption sent ash across the Andes into Argentina, and its summit still glows and steams in the high Atacama desert.
geology: Lascar is part of the volcanic system of Antofagasta. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Parinacota
description: A perfect cone beside Lake Chungará, one of the world's highest lakes, which formed after a landslide about 8,000 years ago dammed a river. Along with neighbouring Pomerape it is known as the Payachatas.
geology: Parinacota is part of the volcanic system of Andes. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Licancabur
description: The crater lake near its 5,900 m summit is one of the highest in the world. It was an Inca ritual site, and NASA scientists have studied the lake as an analogue for ancient Martian lakes.
geology: Licancabur is part of the volcanic system of Andes. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Sabancaya
description: Name means 'tongue of fire' in local languages. Sabancaya, near Colca Canyon, has been erupting since 2016 with regular ash plumes that dust nearby villages and farmland.
geology: Sabancaya is part of the volcanic system of Arequipa. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Ubinas
description: Peru's most active volcano, repeatedly sending ash plumes over highland villages. Eruptions have poisoned grazing land and forced evacuations, and its crater is over a kilometre wide.
geology: Ubinas is part of the volcanic system of Moquegua. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Misti
description: Misti's perfect cone looms over Arequipa, the 'White City', home to around a million people. Inca burials have been found near its summit, and it remains a major hazard to the city.
geology: Misti is part of the volcanic system of Arequipa. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Popocatépetl
description: 'Smoking Mountain' in Nahuatl, rising about 70 km from Mexico City. It has been repeatedly erupting since 1994, and Aztec legend tells of the lovers Popo and Iztaccíhuatl, turned into mountains.
geology: Popocatépetl is part of the volcanic system of Central Mexico. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Colima
description: Mexico's most active volcano, nicknamed the 'Volcán de Fuego'. It stands beside the older, snow-dusted Nevado de Colima, and its explosions have repeatedly forced evacuations of nearby villages.
geology: Colima is part of the volcanic system of Jalisco / Colima. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Pico de Orizaba
description: Mexico's highest mountain and North America's third highest, known to the Aztecs as Citlaltépetl, 'Star Mountain'. It is topped with a glacier and so tall that sailors can see it from the Gulf.
geology: Pico de Orizaba is part of the volcanic system of Puebla / Veracruz. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: El Chichón
description: Overlooked until its 1982 eruption killed about 2,000 villagers in Chiapas. Its sulphur-rich blast injected aerosols into the stratosphere and cooled the global climate for a couple of years.
geology: El Chichón is part of the volcanic system of Chiapas. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Parícutin
description: Parícutin was born in a farmer's cornfield on 20 February 1943 and grew 336 m in a year. It erupted for nine years, burying two villages, with only a church steeple left poking from the lava.
geology: Parícutin is part of the volcanic system of Michoacán. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Lassen Peak
description: One of the largest lava domes in the world, Lassen erupted from 1914 to 1917. It was the only volcano in the contiguous US to erupt before Mount St. Helens in 1980, and its flanks hold steaming hydrothermal fields.
geology: Lassen Peak is part of the volcanic system of California. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Medicine Lake Volcano
description: By volume this is the largest volcano in the Cascades, a broad shield covering around 2,000 square km of northern California. It features glassy obsidian flows and lava-tube caves.
geology: Medicine Lake Volcano is part of the volcanic system of California. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Newberry Volcano
description: A huge shield volcano with a caldera holding two lakes, Paulina and East Lake. Its Big Obsidian Flow, about 1,300 years ago, is a gleaming black field of volcanic glass.
geology: Newberry Volcano is part of the volcanic system of Oregon. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Crater Lake (Mount Mazama)
description: Mount Mazama collapsed around 7,700 years ago after a huge eruption, leaving a caldera filled with snowmelt: the deepest lake in the US at 594 m, and one of the clearest. Wizard Island is a cinder cone inside it.
geology: Crater Lake (Mount Mazama) is part of the volcanic system of Oregon. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Three Sisters
description: Three peaks in Oregon: North, Middle and South Sister. Since the late 1990s the ground near South Sister has bulged upward by tens of centimetres, a sign of magma moving at depth.
geology: Three Sisters is part of the volcanic system of Oregon. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Mount Baker
description: Washington's heavily glaciated Mount Baker briefly alarmed scientists in 1975 when its steam output surged. It also holds the world record for snowfall in a season, with about 1,140 inches in 1998-99.
geology: Mount Baker is part of the volcanic system of Washington. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Glacier Peak
description: A remote peak in the North Cascades that few ever see. Despite its isolation it has a history of large explosive eruptions that spread ash as far as Montana.
geology: Glacier Peak is part of the volcanic system of Washington. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Mount Hood
description: Oregon's highest peak sits only about 80 km from Portland, and steaming fumaroles near Crater Rock hint at what's beneath. Native legend knows it as Wy'east, a warrior turned into a mountain.
geology: Mount Hood is part of the volcanic system of Oregon. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Mount Adams
description: Washington's second-highest volcano, a broad mountain with a dozen glaciers. The Yakama Nation call it Pahto, and it is one of the largest volcanoes in the Cascades.
geology: Mount Adams is part of the volcanic system of Washington. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Long Valley Caldera
description: The caldera formed in a catastrophic eruption 760,000 years ago that deposited the Bishop Tuff, roughly 600 times the volume of Mount St. Helens in 1980. Mammoth Mountain sits on its edge.
geology: Long Valley Caldera is part of the volcanic system of California. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Yellowstone Caldera
description: A supervolcano whose three giant eruptions happened 2.1 million, 1.3 million and 640,000 years ago. Its heat now drives Old Faithful and more than 10,000 hydrothermal features across the park.
geology: Yellowstone Caldera is part of the volcanic system of Wyoming / Montana / Idaho. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Mauna Loa
description: The largest active volcano on Earth by volume, making up half of Hawaii island. It erupted in 2022 for the first time in 38 years, sending lava fountains and flows across its northeast rift.
geology: Mauna Loa is part of the volcanic system of Hawaii. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Mauna Kea
description: Measured from its base on the sea floor, Mauna Kea is more than 10,000 m tall, taller than Everest. Its summit above the clouds hosts world-class observatories and is sacred in Hawaiian culture.
geology: Mauna Kea is part of the volcanic system of Hawaii. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Haleakalā
description: 'House of the Sun' to Hawaiians. Legend says the demigod Maui lassoed the sun from its summit to slow the day, and visitors still gather at its huge crater-like summit depression for sunrise.
geology: Haleakalā is part of the volcanic system of Maui, Hawaii. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Pavlof
description: The most consistently active volcano in the Aleutians. Its eruptions regularly send ash plumes across North Pacific flight routes, and it has produced lava fountains visible from far away.
geology: Pavlof is part of the volcanic system of Alaska Peninsula. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Redoubt
description: In 1989-90 an ash cloud from Redoubt knocked out all four engines of a KLM 747 mid-flight, which dropped thousands of metres before the pilots restarted them. Its 2009 eruption sent ash 19 km high.
geology: Redoubt is part of the volcanic system of Alaska. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Augustine
description: An island volcano in Cook Inlet that erupts repeatedly, in 1976, 1986 and 2006. Its summit periodically collapses, and landslides into the sea can trigger local tsunamis.
geology: Augustine is part of the volcanic system of Alaska. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Katmai
description: In 1912 Novarupta, next to Katmai, produced the largest eruption of the 20th century. The magma drained from beneath Katmai, whose summit collapsed, and ash filled a valley now called the Valley of Ten Thousand Smokes.
geology: Katmai is part of the volcanic system of Alaska. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Great Sitkin
description: Great Sitkin has been repeatedly growing a lava dome in its summit crater. It sits on an Aleutian island near the remote community of Adak.
geology: Great Sitkin is part of the volcanic system of Aleutian Islands. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Cleveland
description: A remote, uninstrumented volcano on uninhabited Chuginadak Island. Sudden explosions can send ash into the flight paths between Asia and North America with little warning.
geology: Cleveland is part of the volcanic system of Aleutian Islands. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Veniaminof
description: An ice-filled caldera about 10 km wide on the Alaska Peninsula, with an active cone inside it. Eruptions melt the ice and send lava flowing across the glacier.
geology: Veniaminof is part of the volcanic system of Alaska Peninsula. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.

name: Mount Warning (Wollumbin)
description: Wollumbin, often translated as 'cloud catcher', is sacred to the Bundjalung people, who ask visitors not to climb it. Its summit is one of the first places on mainland Australia to catch the morning sun.
geology: Mount Warning (Wollumbin) is part of the volcanic system of New South Wales. Its volcanism is associated with the regional tectonic setting and the movement of magma through Earth's crust.
